entities.summary:
Series of wars during the Roman Republic, marking the struggles of enslaved people against their Roman masters, with key events unfolding from 134 BCE to 70 BCE. 

The Servile Wars were a series of uprisings by enslaved people in ancient Italy, triggered by economic hardship and oppressive conditions. 

These wars were sparked by the increasing number of freed slaves, who were seeking equal rights and opportunities. They were also influenced by the growing wealth disparities among Roman citizens, which led to increased tensions between the ruling class and the common people. 

The wars were marked by brutal suppression of the slave uprisings, but also saw the emergence of influential figures like the slave leader, Eunus, who would become a key figure in the history of the region.

The legacy of the Servile Wars can be seen in the gradual decline of the Roman Republic and the rise of the Roman Empire, with the increasing number of freed slaves contributing to the shift in power dynamics.
